chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believers in their reverence, affection and compassion for each other are like one body; when it falls ill, it affects all over with restlessness and fever.

key_terms.الْجَسَدِ: The body (used as a metaphor for the community)
key_terms.تَبَارِّهِمْ: Mutual reverence or respect among them
key_terms.تَرَاحُمِهِمْ: Mutual mercy or compassion among them
key_terms.تَعَاطُفِهِمْ: Mutual empathy or sympathy among them

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic metaphor for the unity and mutual care of believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the organic unity of the Ummah, portraying believers not merely as a community but as a single physiological entity where localized suffering triggers a systemic response of fever and sleeplessness. This hadith, foundational in Shia social ethics, underscores that individual piety is incomplete without communal solidarity, reflecting the concept of 'Tawatur' in spiritual experience where the health of the whole depends on the sensitivity of its parts. It serves as a theological basis for mutual responsibility (Ta'awun) in both material aid and emotional support.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 92. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
The believers in their reverence, affection and compassion for each other are like one body; when it falls ill, it affects all over with restlessness and fever.”
